title: What the slope of a velocity–time graph tells you
examples: How do I find acceleration from a velocity-time graph?
What does the area under a velocity-time graph mean?
What does a flat line on a velocity-time graph mean?

marks.label: 6 s: 12 m/s
marks.ask: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?

explain.say: Imagine you are on a bus in Lagos, pulling away from a stop. Every second, the bus gets 2 metres per second faster. Let us draw that on a velocity–time graph. Velocity means speed in a certain direction.

draw.text: What the slope of a velocity–time graph tells you

marks.label: 6 s: 12 m/s
marks.ask: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?

explain.say: See the yellow dot at the start? Time runs along the bottom, velocity up the side. At zero seconds the bus is at rest, so its velocity is zero. Where do you think the line goes next?

marks.label: 6 s: 12 m/s
marks.ask: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?

explain.say: Up! After 3 seconds the bus is doing 6 metres per second. The line climbs at a steady slope. That slope is the acceleration, which means how much the velocity grows each second. Here it grows by 2 every second.

marks.label: 6 s: 12 m/s
marks.ask: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?

explain.say: At 6 seconds the bus does 12 metres per second. Acceleration is change in velocity divided by time: 12 divided by 6 is 2 metres per second squared. A flat line would mean steady speed. What would a line sloping down mean?

marks.label: 6 s: 12 m/s
marks.ask: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?

explain.say: Slowing down, brilliant! One more secret: the area under the line is the distance. This triangle is half of 6 times 12, so 36 metres. Wow fact: a Formula 1 car reaches 100 kilometres per hour in about 2.6 seconds, so its line would be over five times steeper.

faq.q: How do you find acceleration from a velocity–time graph?
faq.a: Find the gradient: the change in velocity divided by the time it took. A steeper line means a bigger acceleration.
asks: What does the gradient of a velocity-time graph mean?

faq.q: What does a flat line mean on a velocity–time graph?
faq.a: The velocity is not changing, so the object moves at a steady speed. Its acceleration is zero.
asks: horizontal line on a velocity time graph

faq.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph show?
faq.a: The area under the line is the distance travelled. For a triangle, use half times base times height.
asks: How do I find distance from a velocity-time graph?

faq.q: What does a line sloping down mean?
faq.a: The velocity is falling, so the object is slowing down. That is deceleration, or negative acceleration.

faq.q: How is a velocity–time graph different from a distance–time graph?
faq.a: On a distance–time graph the slope is speed. On a velocity–time graph the slope is acceleration and the area is distance. Always read the axis labels first.
asks: difference between distance-time and velocity-time graphs

facts: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time, measured in metres per second squared (m/s²).
The area under a velocity–time graph equals the distance travelled.

quiz.say: A car goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its acceleration?
quiz.show: A car goes from 0 to 20 m/s in 4 s. What is its acceleration?

wrong.0: That multiplies; acceleration is the change in velocity divided by time.
wrong.1: That subtracts 4 from 20; you need 20 divided by 4.

quiz.say: On a velocity–time graph, what does the area under the line give?
quiz.show: On a velocity–time graph, what does the area under the line give?
quiz.why: Velocity times time is distance, so the area under the line is the distance travelled.

wrong.1: Acceleration is the slope of the line, not the area.
wrong.2: Time is read straight off the bottom axis.
